sampling_method:
Every own-result cell in frame_locations was assigned a contiguous 1-based index in reading order, giving a population of 1..483. This paper (ICLR 2022 submission format) is single-column throughout, so PyMuPDF's linear text extraction order is the true reading order with no column-interleaving risk. Location order is strict page order, top-to-bottom; where a subsection's prose and the table it introduces sit on different pages (Appendix F.2's intro prose is on page 22 but Table 15, which it introduces, starts on page 23), the physically earlier page indexes first regardless of which subsection 'owns' the table -- this is why Appendix F.3's one counted cell (page 22) is indexed before Table 15 and Table 16 (page 23) even though F.3 as a subsection follows F.2. Within a table the walk is row-major: printed rows top-to-bottom, left-to-right across that row's own-result columns, skipping baseline rows and hyperparameter columns (Rank r, # Trainable Parameters, weight-type labels) in between. No table in this paper prints a caption-level delta the way ELECTRA's Table 1 caption did, so no location's count includes a caption cell.

Ownership. Tables 2, 3 and 4's citation baselines are marked '*' ('* indicates numbers published in prior works', Table 2's and Table 3's captions) and are excluded; rows marked with a dagger are, per Table 2's caption, 'runs configured in a setup similar to Houlsby et al. (2019) for a fair comparison' -- the authors' own reimplementation of a prior baseline under a matched protocol, hence own results despite naming a prior method (RoBlarge (AdptP) dagger, RoBlarge (AdptH) dagger, RoBlarge (LoRA) dagger; the dagger is spelled out in this file to keep it plain ASCII). Table 2 prints 'RoBlarge (LoRA)' at 0.8M twice, once without and once with the dagger, with different digits in MRPC/QNLI/RTE/STS-B/Avg -- Section 5.2 explains these are two different evaluation protocols (the dagger run restricts sequence length and MRPC/RTE/STS-B initialization to match Houlsby et al. (2019)), not a duplicate print, so both rows are counted separately as own. Table 4 (GPT-3, page 8) prints no '*' or dagger anywhere, and its surrounding prose gives no citation for WikiSQL/MNLI-m/SAMSum at this scale, so every row is own; Table 8 (Appendix A, page 17) is the one place ownership is per cell rather than per row within a single method name: its 'GPT-3 Few-Shot' row states RTE is 'taken... from the GPT-3 paper (Brown et al., 2020)' (a citation, excluded) while the same row's MNLI-m entry is the authors' own eval ('For MNLI-matched, we use two demonstrations per class...'), so that row contributes 1 of its 2 cells.

Tables 13, 14, 15, 16 and 18 (Appendices F and H) print no '*' and no dagger anywhere -- confirmed against the rendered page images (p21, p22, p23, p26), not assumed from the absent text-extracted glyph alone, because the bolding these tables use to mark the best score per column also does not survive text extraction, and the two needed to be told apart visually. Table 14's caption states this explicitly ('less than 0.01 for all the experiments we ran'); Table 13's caption is worded more thinly ('...for all adaption approaches'), but its intro prose ('We also repeat our experiment on DART and WebNLG following the setup of Li & Liang (2021)') and the total absence of any citation marker on the Fine-Tune/AdapterL/FTTop2/PrefLayer rows that carry '*' in Tables 2 and 3 support the same reading: these appendix tables are complete own reruns, including the Fine-Tune and prior-method rows, distinct from the body tables (2, 3) where the identical method names are baselines. This is the single largest judgement call in this file, since Tables 13 and 14 alone are 132 of the 483 cells; it is recorded here so it can be checked.

Value convention. GLUE/E2E/DART/WebNLG-style cells print 'mean+/-std over seeds/trials' (e.g. '70.4+/-.1', '1449.4+/-0.8'); per this set's convention the point value is the cell and the +/- figure is not separately indexed. Table 5's and Table 6's '(+/-0.5%)'/'(+/-0.1%)' annotations are printed once per row label, not per cell ('we report [it] in the first column' -- Table 5's caption), so they are a stated measurement precision for the whole row and are not a cell. Table 4's caption states a similar once-per-table fluctuation band and is excluded on the same footing. Table 13/14's MET and TER values print without a leading zero ('.39', '.46'); JSON requires a leading zero for a numeric literal, so any such value is stored as e.g. 0.39, with the print convention noted on the label it applies to.

Split tokens. WebNLG's Table 14 prints three sub-columns (U/S/A -- unseen/seen/all categories, per its own caption) under each of BLEU/MET/TER; these are three already-separate printed cells, not one combined token, so no splitting judgement is needed there (unlike SAMSum's 'R1/R2/RL' in Table 4, which is one token for three metrics and is split into three cells per this set's rule). Table 4's SAMSum column ('52.0/28.0/44.5') is exactly that combined-token case and contributes 3 cells per row, one per Rouge variant.

Exclusions. Ratios and multipliers describing parameter/compute/memory budgets ('reduce... by 10,000 times', 'GPU memory requirement by 3 times', 'up to 2/3', 'up to 3 times', the '(+2.2%)' printed beside an already-counted absolute latency in Table 1, '21.5 ~= 6.91/0.32' in Section 7.3, and the restated 'as large as 20'/'only around 2' in Section H.4) are excluded throughout, matching this set's treatment of ELECTRA's '30x more compute'/'1/20th the parameters': a resource-budget ratio is not a performance delta and is excluded regardless of whether an absolute is printed beside it, whereas an absolute speed/latency/memory figure presented as an outcome is counted as a result (Table 1's per-cell latencies; Section 4.2's VRAM/checkpoint-size worked example for GPT-3 175B -- 1.2TB, 350GB, 35MB; footnote 5's two throughput figures, 32.5 and 43.1 tokens/s) and a genuine delta with no absolute printed beside it in that instance is counted once per printed instance ('a 25% speedup during training on GPT-3 175B compared to full fine-tuning' has no absolute alongside it in that sentence, and is a different figure from footnote 5's own ratio of 43.1/32.5 = +32.6%, so the two are not the same claim restated and both are counted). Section 7.1's '18M (roughly 35MB if stored in FP16)' and Table 5's header '# of Trainable Parameters = 18M' are the parameter budget the ablation is run under, i.e. hyperparameter, not result, matching this file's uniform exclusion of every '# Trainable Parameters'/'|Theta|' column in Tables 1-4, 13-16 -- LoRA-specific instruction: this column is a headline number in the paper's own framing but is still an architecture/parameter-count spec, and is recorded as hyperparameter throughout, never silently dropped from this note.

Restated values. Appendix F.3 states 'PrefixEmbed performing only slightly better than random chance (37.6% vs. 33.3%)': 37.6 is an exact restatement of Table 16's PrefixEmbed/MNLI-100 cell and, per this set's rule that each printed instance is its own cell (established for ELECTRA's thrice-printed 'five points' delta), it counts again at its own location; 33.3% is 1/3 restated as a percentage ('random chance' for 3-way NLI) with no producing run behind it, so it is not own-result and is not indexed at all (excluded outright, not merely marked unconfident).

Table 7 (page 12, Frobenius norms of projected weight matrices at GPT-3's 48th layer) is this file's least certain role call: role is limited to result/hyperparameter/dataset_statistic, and a matrix-norm diagnostic from the authors' own trained model fits none cleanly; by elimination, and because it is the authors' own empirical measurement presented as a finding ('We draw several conclusions from Table 7...'), it is counted as result, but every cell drawn from it is marked confident:false, matching ELECTRA's precedent for its Appendix G footnote 10 (a measured property whose role was the least certain judgement in that file).

labels.notes: Table 7: 'The Frobenius norm of U^T Wq V^T where U and V are the left/right top r singular vector directions of either (1) DeltaWq, (2) Wq, or (3) a random matrix. Own by construction (their own trained GPT-3+LoRA weights; no citation applies to an internal analysis table). Marked confident:false because role is genuinely unclear: the schema limits role to result/hyperparameter/dataset_statistic, and a matrix-norm diagnostic used to support an interpretability claim ('DeltaW amplifies some features that are already in W') does not sit as comfortably under 'result' as a benchmark accuracy does -- see sampling_method for the full reasoning and the ELECTRA footnote-10 precedent this follows.
